skill.name: perplexity-search
skill.description: Use Perplexity models through OpenRouter and LiteLLM to search current web information, compare sources, and return grounded answers with citations.
skill.summary: Search current web sources using Perplexity models through OpenRouter.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, model terminology, public setup URLs, or safe configuration checks. Confirmed issues remain around plaintext OpenRouter key handling in setup guidance and scripts, unrestricted local output writes, and third-party disclosure of user queries.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer a user secret manager or existing environment variable. If writing .env files, create them with restrictive permissions and clear warnings.
Do not print full export commands containing real keys. Show a placeholder or a masked value after setup.
Document that queries are sent to OpenRouter and Perplexity. Warn users not to submit secrets, regulated data, or confidential records.
Warn before overwriting files, resolve paths carefully, or restrict saved results to a user-approved workspace location.

content.user_title: Search Current Web Sources with Perplexity
content.value_statement: Current facts and recent research are hard to verify from a static model alone. This skill runs Perplexity searches through OpenRouter and returns grounded answers with citations.
actual_capabilities: Runs Perplexity Sonar searches from a local Python CLI.
Selects Sonar, Sonar Pro, Sonar Pro Search, and reasoning models.
Checks whether LiteLLM and OPENROUTER_API_KEY are configured.
Returns answers with token usage and available citation metadata.
Saves search results to a JSON file when requested.
Provides setup, model selection, and query strategy references.
limitations: Requires a paid OpenRouter account and a valid API key.
Sends search queries to OpenRouter and Perplexity services.
Citation availability depends on the model response returned by LiteLLM.
Saved outputs may contain sensitive query text or generated answers.

use_cases.title: Track Recent Literature
use_cases.description: Find recent papers, clinical updates, and source-backed summaries for a defined research question.

use_cases.title: Verify Current Technical Guidance
use_cases.description: Check recent library behavior, deployment guidance, or API changes before coding decisions.

use_cases.title: Compare Current Options
use_cases.description: Gather current evidence across tools, treatments, or technologies with model and source control.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Current Fact Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one current answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use perplexity-search to answer: [question]. Prefer recent sources and summarize the key evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Literature Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use perplexity-search with sonar-pro for [topic]. Focus on peer-reviewed work from [years] and list strongest findings.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Use perplexity-search to compare [option A] and [option B] for [context]. Include costs, risks, and cited evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run staged perplexity-search queries for [complex topic]: overview, recent updates, limitations, and consensus. Synthesize conflicts and confidence.

output_examples.input: A user asks for the latest FDA guidance on a therapy.
output_examples.output: A concise answer with current guidance, key dates, cited sources, and a note about clinical verification.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether a library changed its authentication flow.
output_examples.output: A source-backed summary of recent documentation, migration concerns, and links to official references.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for recent CAR-T trial evidence.
output_examples.output: A literature-oriented summary with trial names, outcomes, limitations, and citations when returned.

best_practices: Keep queries specific with topic, date range, sources, and expected output.
Use cheaper models for simple lookups and stronger models for multi-step synthesis.
Review citations and avoid submitting secrets, patient data, or private company information.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, credentials, or confidential records into search queries.
Do not use broad prompts when a narrow evidence question is available.
Do not treat generated answers as final medical, legal, or financial advice.

faq.question: Does this require a Perplexity account?
faq.answer: No. It uses Perplexity models through OpenRouter with an OpenRouter API key.

faq.question: Which model is the default?
faq.answer: The CLI defaults to Sonar Pro unless a different supported model is selected.

faq.question: Can it save results?
faq.answer: Yes. The script can write search results to a local output file when requested.

faq.question: Does it access the internet?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends search requests through LiteLLM to OpenRouter and Perplexity.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Queries leave the local machine, so avoid secrets and regulated data.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
